items.followUp: Why are elements of groups 13 and 14 called p-block elements?

rubric.why: The block of an element is determined by the subshell into which its last electron enters.
rubric.description: States that the last electron enters an s orbital or subshell.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying the s subshell as the destination of the last electron.

rubric.why: This connects the electron configuration of these groups to their block classification.
rubric.description: Concludes that elements of groups 1 and 2 are called s-block elements.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for linking groups 1 and 2 with the s-block.

modelAnswer: In elements of groups 1 and 2, the last electron enters an s orbital.
Therefore, these elements are called s-block elements.

items.followUp: Define crystalline solids and give two examples.

rubric.why: Amorphous solids lack the regular arrangement of particles found in crystalline solids.
rubric.description: Defines amorphous solids by stating that their particles are not arranged in a regular pattern.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for describing the irregular arrangement of particles.

rubric.why: Suitable examples demonstrate recognition of amorphous solids.
rubric.description: Gives one or more examples of amorphous solids.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a suitable example such as glass, plastic, or rubber.

modelAnswer: Amorphous solids are solids whose particles are not arranged in a regular, orderly pattern.
Examples include glass, plastic, and rubber.

items.followUp: How can a saturated solution be prepared by heating and cooling?

rubric.why: Heating allows more solute to dissolve and is used to prepare the hot saturated solution.
rubric.description: Describes heating the solvent and adding solute until a hot saturated solution is formed.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating the heating and dissolving step.

rubric.why: Careful cooling without disturbance can leave more solute dissolved than is normally soluble at the lower temperature.
rubric.description: States that the hot saturated solution is cooled slowly without disturbance to produce a supersaturated solution.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the careful cooling step and its result.

modelAnswer: Heat the solvent and add solute until no more dissolves, making a hot saturated solution.
Cool the solution slowly without disturbance; the resulting solution is supersaturated.
